data.narrative:
Summit Lithium Technologies is a Series A-stage climate and energy company founded by Amanda Hall that has raised approximately C$120M to date. The comparable universe for lithium-focused frontier tech includes one public peer (ticker LNZA) and eight private-sector companies spanning battery materials and energy storage, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy segment—while eight sector peers exist, fewer than three met the criteria for direct valuation triangulation. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the C$120M raised baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $240M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $204M to $276M (median $240M), centered on the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficiently granular peer data at the same stage and valuation tier, which limits confidence in relative-value calibration. The range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the median estimate. Investors should note that this valuation is anchored primarily to fundraising history rather than comparable transaction multiples, reflecting the nascent and heterogeneous nature of the frontier lithium technology landscape.
